title: Purity for the punctured spectrum of a regular local ring
statement: Let A be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of Krull dimension at least two [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let U be the open complement of its closed point in Spec A [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Every finite etale morphism Y -> U [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism] extends to a finite etale morphism F -> Spec A together with an isomorphism Y to its restriction to U over U.

source.place: Tag 0BMA, pione-lemma-purity-regular, assertion (1); Tags 0BM9 and 0BLM for the normal-algebra and lifting criteria

proof.text: Induct on the finite dimension. Regularity gives normality. For a connected cover, Tag 0BM9 constructs B as the integral closure of A in its finite separable function field, a finite normal domain extending the cover. Prove B etale; use finite disjoint unions for disconnected covers.

In dimension two, going down gives dimension two at maximal ideals of the finite normal algebra. Serre normality gives depth two there. Miracle flatness over the regular base makes the finite algebra flat. Tag 0BJH, the flat quasi-finite depth-two purity criterion, makes it etale.

In higher dimension choose a regular parameter f outside the square of the maximal ideal. The quotient is regular of dimension one less. Induction extends the restricted punctured cover over the quotient. Regular parameters give depth A equal to its dimension, hence at least three; f is a nonzerodivisor. These verify the hypotheses of Tag 0BLM, which lifts this extension to the original cover. Empty covers extend to the empty scheme.

theorem exists_finite_etale_extension_of_regular_local_punctured_spectrum
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsRegularLocalRing A]
    (hdim : (2 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim A)
    (U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens)
    (hU : ∀ x : Spec (.of A), x ∈ U ↔ x ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint A)
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (q : Y ⟶ U.toScheme) [IsFinite q] [Etale q] :
    ∃ (F : Scheme.{u}) (r : F ⟶ Spec (.of A)), IsFinite r ∧ Etale r ∧
      ∃ e : Y ≅ (r ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme, e.hom ≫ r ∣_ U = q
